subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally treat `/exec` as persistent session state, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy can be shadowed by older session values.

options.title: Make global policy the upper bound
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields that exceed the current global or agent policy, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep session persistence
options.body: Document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing channel lanes.

options.title: Add explicit reset first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing runtime precedence semantics.

recommendation.title: Make global policy the upper bound
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields that exceed the current global or agent policy, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the clearest history on the original `/exec` session override feature and current exec-default resolver behavior.
